target_customer: Enterprise and mid-market companies with high support volume across email, chat, phone, SMS and WhatsApp (customers named include Print.com, Mollie, Viva, TicketSwap, MoneyGram)
problem: Support teams are overloaded with repetitive and complex cases across many channels. Open sells an AI agent that resolves interactions end to end, with handoff to humans, and says it automates about 77% of interactions on average.
business_model: Usage-based per automated resolution (site lists $0.90 per resolution, no per-seat fee)
product_category: AI customer support and communication platform

founders.name: Mohammad Gharbat
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the founder. A Dutch headline (Silicon Canals) calls him a former Mollie employee; not confirmed from an opened source, so not recorded as an employer. An Arabic report names Mohammad Tabbaza as co-founder, but the YC page and company sources do not, so he is not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM agents over support channels, voice and integrations with helpdesks are standard but demanding engineering; the company claims ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II, which takes work for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and enterprise security certification help, but the category attracted well funded rivals and agents are largely built on shared model APIs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Helpdesk incumbents and funded AI agent startups were all shipping AI resolution products; later coverage (2026) shows heavily funded Sierra and Decagon. No acquisition of Open found.

market_need_then: Support is a large labor cost and generative AI made automated resolution feasible in 2023 and 2024. The YC page lists enterprise customers in production, which suggests early demand in Europe.

branding.domain_note: Uses open.cx; the .cx top level gives a short name, and the earlier name OpenCX is visible in GitHub org opencx-labs. Dates not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and promotional, emphasizing reliability, enterprise security and human handoff.

rebrands.why: Third party profiles say 'Open, formerly OpenCX'; no source states the date or reason.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional trade press covered the funding rounds, but the name 'Open' is generic and collides with OpenAI and OpenX in search results.

outcome_analysis: Open is an active Amman-based YC Winter 2024 company that reached enterprise customers in Europe, raised a $1.52M pre-seed in January 2025 and a $7M seed in January 2026 with YC and Gulf investors. It claims 77% automation of interactions and security certifications. It competes in a very crowded and well funded AI support category, so the outcome is still open.
notes: Pre-seed amount of $1.52M reported by Silicon Canals, The AI Insider and CoinTurk; investor list from the Silicon Canals headline. Seed confirmed by the company post (January 2026) and Middle East AI News; one aggregator lists $8.5M total or a Series A, which conflicts and is not recorded. Total raised not stated by the company. Customer names and the 77% figure are self reported. Headquarters conflicts (Amman per YC, Dubai or San Francisco in other sources).
